Catholic Life
Prayer and Worship
Prayer and Worship
Prayer is an important part of the spiritual life of our school and children are introduced to a carefully planned range of prayers as they progress from EYFS to Year 6. This page contains the prayers that children will encounter and learn during their time at school, providing families with an easy way to practise and pray them together at home. Simply sharing a few quiet moments together, reading a prayer aloud or encouraging your child to lead can make a meaningful difference. Using the same prayers at home and at school helps children grow in confidence, deepen their understanding of the Catholic faith and see prayer as a natural way to give thanks, ask for help, say sorry and spend time with God.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to
Holy Family Catholic Primary School
Per ardua ad astra
Catholic Life
Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching
The Gospel of Jesus Christ on the Street
At Holy Family Catholic Primary School, Catholic Social Teaching is part of who we are and how we live each day. Inspired by the Gospel of Jesus Christ, we encourage our children to love, serve, and care for others both in school and in the wider world. Catholic Social Teaching helps children understand that faith is lived through our actions. We want every child to recognise their God-given value and to know they can make a positive difference through kindness, fairness, respect, and service.
Catholic Social Teaching is woven throughout our whole curriculum. Through the topics children study in Science, Humanities, and the texts they explore in Literacy lessons, each area of learning is linked to a Catholic Social Teaching theme and question. This helps children make meaningful connections between their faith and the world around them, ensuring that Catholic Social Teaching is not something taught separately alongside RE, but a thread running through all areas of school life and learning.
The principles of Catholic Social Teaching are also reflected in our prayer life and wider school community. Through Religious Education, Celebration of the Word, assemblies, fundraising, and acts of service, children are encouraged to put their faith into action and follow Jesus by loving and serving others.
Through charity work, supporting local and global causes, caring for the environment, and responding to the needs of others with kindness and empathy, our children learn how to live out these teachings every day. At Holy Family, we want every child to know they can be a force for good in the world - following Jesus by helping to build a community of justice, peace, and love.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission Statement | The Holy Family Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to
Holy Family Catholic Primary School
Per ardua ad astra
Mission Statement
Mission Statement
Achieving personal excellence for ourselves and the glory of God.
Our Mission Statement ensures that Christ is at the centre of all the work within our school.
Our Mission Statement is not simply a mantra that is repeated by children and staff or something that is just displayed around our school. The staff, children, parents and Governors work hard to ensure that everyone within our school community is able to achieve personal excellence so that our Mission Statement is lived out daily.
As a Catholic school it is imperative that we strive for excellence for ourselves, the children and colleagues. It ensures that we recognise the uniqueness of the individual, made in God's image and loved by him. The search for excellence is also an integral part of the spiritual quest.
We believe that our Mission Statement will only be lived out by a clear commitment to high expectations and ensuring that the love of God is present in our school.
We know that children and staff will only achieve personal excellence in an environment where they feel respected, valued and loved. Everyone in our school has a responsibility to ensure that the Gospel values are evident in our school in all the interactions that take place and that they underpin all the policies in place.
As a Catholic school we recognise that the children in our school are unique, made in the image of God and divine. Once we recognise this, how can we not have the very highest expectations of them and each other? In a loving and nurturing environment, we know that we can challenge one another and the children so that we can all achieve our very best. It is in this way that we hope the Holy Family School community can give glory to God.
Our Mission Statement is reviewed regularly by staff, children, parents and governors. This ensures that we remain rooted in the mission of the Church.
I am writing to you to tell you about our School Mission Statement and to explain why we think it is helpful and very powerful. A school Mission Statement is there to guide everyone in a school and show the world what that school considers important. This helps to make schools distinctive so that they stand out from one another. It also gives everyone in the school community a shared purpose and common goal.
When we try to 'achieve personal excellence', it reminds us about something very important. In the book of Genesis we learn that we are made by God and made in the image of God. We are all divine. Therefore, each of us has been blessed with amazing talents and we are capable of achieving excellence. We are children of God - of course we can achieve excellence! If we settled for less than our best or were happy not trying to achieve excellence then we would be letting God and ourselves down. By aiming to achieve excellence, we can grow to become the person that God wants us to be. Saint Henry Newman wrote that God has a 'definite purpose' for each of us. We may not know what that purpose is but if we want to fulfil the purpose that God has set out for us, then we should always be striving to achieve excellence. The word 'personal' in our Mission Statement has a truly important meaning for all of us at Holy Family. It shows us all and is a daily reminder that we are all unique. We have different skills and talents. The 'excellence' that we achieve may look different to another persons but we can always achieve 'personal excellence'.
When we achieve personal excellence, we do not only please our parents - we also please God. When we have struggled and really tried our best to achieve excellence then we can feel proud and pleased. This makes us feel good and helps us to grow as people because we become more confident. Doing well and achieving excellence is an amazing feeling - the best! This is why our Mission Statement says that we are achieving personal excellence for 'ourselves'. At the same time as doing it for ourselves we are also giving glory to God. We are showing the world how magnificent God's creation is. We are praising and thanking God every time we achieve excellence. At Holy Family, we always make sure that God's light is always shining through our achievements.
Thank you for reading my letter. I hope that you now understand why we think our Mission Statement is so good. We feel very fortunate to have a Mission Statement that helps all of us - teachers and children - live in a way that pleases God.

Catholic Life
Links with our Parish Church
Links with our Parish Church
Father Neil is the Parish Priest at Holy Family Catholic Church. He visits the school regularly to celebrate Mass with us and to support our RE learning and the liturgical life of the school. Our strong partnership with Father Neil plays an important role in helping the children develop their understanding of the Catholic faith and the liturgical year.
Key Stage 2 classes attend Mass regularly with parishioners, as well as on Holy Days of Obligation. The children are given opportunities to take part by reading and serving at the altar during these celebrations. On Holy Days, Father Neil also invites our younger children into the church for a special age-appropriate service.
During both Lent and Advent, children in Years 4–6 are invited to receive the Sacrament of Reconciliation with Father Neil. Our oldest pupils are also given the opportunity to spend time with him in a question-and-answer session, helping them to deepen their understanding of their faith and grow in their relationship with God.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome | The Holy Family Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to
Holy Family Catholic Primary School
Per ardua ad astra
Welcome
'Holy Family is an outstanding Catholic school, valued by all members of its community who are committed to living their mission of ‘Achieving excellence for the glory of God’.
'Outstanding' Section 48 Inspection – May 2023
On behalf of everyone at Holy Family Catholic Primary School I would like to welcome you to our website. This website is a window into what we do and what we are about. After browsing through, you will hopefully have gained an insight into life at Holy Family.
If you are viewing our website as a prospective parent, pupil or staff member, please know that Holy Family is a school that prides itself on its warm welcome. We have a great deal to offer but recognise that every child, family and member of staff helps us to grow, develop and continue to flourish.
Our school only opened in 2012 and we are immensely proud of all that has been achieved since then: ‘Outstanding’ OfSTED Inspection (2014 and 2024); two ‘Outstanding’ Section 48 Inspections (2016 and 2023) and school data that consistently places the school significantly above national and local authority averages. We are a very popular school within the local area and beyond, with waiting lists for all our classes.
We are highly successful because there is a commitment from the whole school community to living out our Mission Statement – ‘Achieving personal excellence for ourselves and the glory of God.’ This Mission Statement underpins all that we do at Holy Family.
We recognise that every child entrusted into our care is a divine creation, made in the image of God. Pupils at Holy Family know that they are loved and valued. As a result, we are able to have the very highest expectations for our pupils (and staff). Our pupils are happy and feel safe in our school environment and so we are able to expect the best from them. By marrying together an environment based on the teachings of Jesus Christ and our high expectations, our children can truly flourish and achieve personal excellence.
It is a privilege to lead a Catholic school and I am very fortunate to work alongside exceptional staff and dedicated governors. We serve a highly supportive parent body who work collaboratively with the school to ensure the best outcomes for our children.
I would be delighted to welcome you to see our school in action or share more information with you, please do not hesitate to contact me directly (head@holyfamily.ealing.sch.uk) if I can be of any assistance.
'Holy Family Catholic Primary School is a place where pupils thrive.'
'Outstanding' Ofsted Inspection - May 2024

Catholic Life
Prayer and Worship
School Prayers
Nursery and Reception
Nursery and Reception
In EYFS, children are gently introduced to prayer through short, simple and familiar words. Across the year, they learn to make the Sign of the Cross, join in with simple responses such as “Amen”, say thank you to God, say sorry, and ask God for help. These prayers are linked to the Church year, for example waiting for Jesus during Advent, giving thanks at Christmas, saying sorry during Lent and celebrating the joy of Easter. As children become more confident, they are encouraged to join in independently and begin using their own words to pray.
